title: Boot API Design: Controllers That Hold
objective: After this lesson you will be able to design sync JSON endpoints, SSE streaming endpoints with event shapes, and validated tool endpoints with idempotency and audit — following HTTP semantics strictly.
why: The API is the product seam every client (web, mobile, future integrations) builds against: method semantics, streaming shapes, validation errors, and idempotency determine whether clients are robust or brittle. Mutations on GET, unvalidated bodies, and unkeyed money endpoints are contract violations with production consequences — designed here, enforced always.

blocks.text: Sync JSON: validated in, shaped out

Controllers validate bodies (Jakarta constraints + explicit checks), return contract-shaped entities (Ch.4 Spring course), and error with structured envelopes (code/message/details, never stacks). Validation failures are 400s with field-level reasons — clients fix requests instead of guessing. OpenAPI generated from code (springdoc) keeps docs truthful by construction.

Streaming endpoints emit **typed frames** (`token`, `citations`, `done`, `error`) as Server-Sent Events with Last-Event-ID resume support: versioned event names (Ch.1 contracts), heartbeat comments for proxy survival, and completion envelopes (final entity + usage). Untyped newline streams force clients to guess framing — frames make streaming a protocol, not a hope.
Tool endpoints: POST, validated, keyed, audited

Mutations ride **POST** (never GET — crawlers/prefetch trigger GETs): validated bodies, idempotency keys required on money paths, audit entries per call (who/args/verdict/outcome). Reads stay GET (cacheable, safe). Method semantics protect against the entire class of accidental invocation — REST constraints as safety features.

blocks.title: Classify the endpoints
blocks.note: Run it: expect sound, then three violations named precisely (GET-mutation, unkeyed-money, untyped-stream). Method semantics audited mechanically per endpoint.

items: Sync: validated bodies, shaped entities, structured errors, OpenAPI-generated docs
SSE: versioned typed frames + resume + heartbeats + completion envelopes
Mutations on POST with keys + audit; reads on GET; violations named per endpoint

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice classifier on all five endpoints and map verdicts. (b) Write the SSE frame list for a chat reply (token/citations/done/error) with one field each. (c) State the idempotency-key rule for refunds vs reads in one sentence each.
hints: Verdicts: sound / GET-mutation / unkeyed-money / sound-keyed / untyped-stream (in order).
Frames: token{text}, citations[list], done{entity, usage}, error{code, message} — versioned names.
Refunds: keys required (recovery duplicates); reads: keyless (safe by method).
exercise.why: Method-semantics auditing (per-endpoint verdicts), frame design (versioned typed events), and key rules (money keyed, reads free) are the three API judgments.
exercise.code: // Endpoint-audit pattern: method × mutation × keys × frames checked.

quiz.q: Refund endpoint on GET for convenience. Verdict?
options: Violation: crawlers/prefetch trigger GETs — mutations ride POST with keys + audit, always
quiz.explain: Method semantics are safety features: GET must be side-effect free. Convenience that executes on prefetch is an incident class.

quiz.q: SSE stream of bare newline-separated text. Gap?
options: Untyped frames: clients guess boundaries/versions/errors — versioned typed frames + resume make streaming a protocol
quiz.explain: Framing contracts (names, versions, resume, completion) turn streams from hopes into protocols clients can robustly consume.

quiz.q: Idempotency keys on read endpoints. Verdict?
options: Unnecessary: GET reads are safe by method — keys belong on mutating money paths, not cacheable reads
quiz.explain: Keys cost complexity: spend on mutations (duplicate charges), skip on safe reads. Method semantics already protect GETs.

summary: Validated sync bodies, versioned SSE frames with resume, POST mutations with keys + audit. HTTP semantics as safety features, audited per endpoint.
next: Surface shaped — now identity: JWT sessions, thread ownership, and tenant isolation that never trusts IDs. Next: auth that holds.
